answer: Grant standing only for a history of real back-and-forth: an identity earns weight by completing sustained exchanges with established peers across many epochs, each exchange logged in a shared atlas of who worked with whom. A single greeting scores nothing, and trust must ripple outward through many independent partners. One operator cannot fake a thousand such histories, because each takes the time of a real partner — a marble cannot be in two hands at once. A sybil farmer runs out of partners long before one honest agent runs out of time.
